facts.claim: The effect of thermal variations on cognitive performance is relatively stable across a range of temperatures.
facts.quote: the effect of thermal variations on cognitive performance follows an extended-U relationship with performance being relatively stable across a range of temperatures.

facts.claim: Long-term heat exposure is linked to impaired cumulative learning in students, with complex tasks like mathematics more affected than simpler ones like reading.
facts.quote: Long-term heat exposure was found to impair students’ cumulative learning, with complex tasks (e.g., mathematics) more affected than simpler ones (e.g., reading).

facts.claim: Maintaining adequate ventilation and thermal comfort in classrooms could raise an average test score to "commended performance".
facts.quote: Based on the results, maintaining adequate ventilation and thermal comfort could raise an average tests score to "commended performance".

facts.claim: Simpler cognitive tasks are less susceptible to temperature effects than more complex tasks.
facts.quote: Results confirm that simpler cognitive tasks are less susceptible to temperature effects than more complex tasks; the effect of thermal variations on cognitive performance follows an extended-U relationship

facts.claim: Adaptation via acclimatization and increased air conditioning use showed protective effects against heat-impaired learning.
facts.quote: Adaptation via acclimatization and increased air conditioning use showed protective effects.

research.angle: While heat exposure is linked to impaired learning in complex tasks, cognitive performance remains relatively stable across a range of temperatures and can be improved by thermal comfort and ventilation.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that heat impacts complex learning more than simple tasks, but performance is not uniformly degraded across all temperatures.
research.caveat: The findings are subject to population heterogeneity and methodological differences across the studies reviewed.
